key_insight: US clinical trials that require English proficiency tend to enroll fewer Asian and Hispanic/Latinx participants, while explicit language accommodation is uncommon.
clinical_relevance: Language eligibility criteria are a modifiable trial-design feature that may influence who gets enrolled and therefore how representative trial populations are.
method: Cross-sectional analysis of 44,487 US interventional trials on ClinicalTrials.gov with posted results.
Free-text eligibility criteria were mined with validated regular expressions to detect English-language requirements and language accommodation.
Associations with enrolled racial and ethnic composition were estimated using adjusted generalized linear models.
evidence_signal: Among trials with exclusively US sites, 12.9% included an English-language requirement and 1.8% documented language accommodation; the requirement was associated with lower enrolled proportions of Asian and Hispanic/Latinx participants.
watch_item: Because many trials lacked complete race/ethnicity reporting and the study is observational, the findings show association rather than proving that language criteria caused enrollment differences.
paper_title: Language eligibility criteria and enrolled racial and ethnic composition in US clinical trials: a cross-sectional study
